name: Treaty with the Wea and Kickapoo, 1816
nations: Wea (today within the Peoria Tribe of Indians of Oklahoma)
Kickapoo (today the Kickapoo Tribe in Kansas, the Kickapoo Tribe of Oklahoma and the Kickapoo Traditional Tribe of Texas)
promises: Article 2: the tribes acknowledged the treaty of Greenville (1795) and their later treaties.
Article 3: the tribes confirmed the surveyed boundary of the land on the Wabash and White rivers ceded in 1809.
Article 4: the Kickapoo acknowledged their cession of the tract between that line, the Wabash and the Vermillion River under their treaty of December 9, 1809.
landTaken: Royce Areas 71, 73 and 74 are attached to this id; they were ceded by the 1809 treaties, which this treaty confirmed (Royce; Docket 317 findings, 1962).
today: This treaty took no new land and promised no payment. The Commission's findings on the land it confirmed belong to the 1809 treaties: it found the consideration for Royce Area 71 unconscionable (Dockets 253, 131 and 314-D, 1969), and the Kickapoo recovered in Docket 317 (1970). Those are recorded under kappler-109, kappler-111 and kappler-112, not here.

openQuestions: The 1969 opinion says Docket 317 was dismissed from that proceeding because the Kickapoo were interested only in Royce Area 73, yet Docket 317 ended in a 1970 award on stipulation; the basis of that award was not traced.
No Wea, Peoria or Kickapoo account of the 1816 treaty was found.

2026-11-08 sweep: Court of Claims and ICC full text searched for Wea and Kickapoo (Court of Claims index; 26 Ct. Cl. 323 of 1891 and the 1966-67 Kickapoo appeals) and 'Wea Kickapoo 1816' (ICC); nothing new.

nationVoice.nation: Peoria Tribe of Indians of Oklahoma
nationVoice.summary: The Tribe's history says the Peoria, Kaskaskia, Piankeshaw and Wea, united as the Confederated Peoria in 1854, were forced from ancestral lands in Illinois, Indiana, Michigan, Ohio, Iowa and Missouri, moved to Missouri, then Kansas, then northeastern Oklahoma, and by 1915 held no tribal land at all.
